messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Kaj kiel tiu kiu kun elĉerpita spiro, eliris el la maro al la bordo, turnas sin al la danĝera akvo kaj rigardas,

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (to English) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------|--------| | **E** | Coordinating conjunction linking to previous clause | **Kaj** | “and” | OK | | **come** | Comparative particle “as, like” | **kiel** | “as/like” | OK | | **quei** | Demonstrative pronoun, plural, “those” (generic) | **tiu** | “that one” (singular generic) | OK | | **che** | Relative pronoun “who” | **kiu** | “who” | OK | | **con** | Preposition “with” (instrumental) | **kun** | “with” | OK | | **lena** | Noun “breath” (archaic) | **spiro** | “breath” | OK | | **affannata** | Past participle adjective “spent, exhausted” | **elĉerpita** | “exhausted” | OK | | **uscito** | Verb “issued, came out” (past participle used as verb) | **eliris** | “went out, emerged” | OK | | **fuor** | Preposition “out of” (archaic form of *fuori*) | **el** | “out of” | OK | | **del** | Preposition + article “of the” (genitive) – not required in Esperanto because the “out of” relation is already expressed by **el** | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | **pelago** | Noun “sea, ocean” | **maro** | “sea” | OK | | **a** | Preposition “to, toward” | **al** | “to, toward” | OK | | **la** (before *riva*) | Definite article “the” | **la** | “the” | OK | | **riva** | Noun “shore, bank” | **bordo** | “shore, bank” | OK | | **si** | Reflexive pronoun (3rd person) | **sin** | “himself/herself” | OK | | **volge** | Verb “turns, directs oneself” | **turnas** | “turns” | OK | | **a** (second occurrence) | Preposition “to, toward” | **al** | “to, toward” | OK | | **l'acqua** | Noun “the water” (with article) | **akvo** | “water” | OK | | **perigliosa** | Adjective “perilous, dangerous” | **danĝera** | “dangerous” | OK | | **e** | Coordinating conjunction “and” | **kaj** | “and” | OK | | **guata** | Verb “gazes, looks at” | **rigardas** | “looks at, gazes” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: **del** – the genitive “of the” is not needed in Esperanto because the preposition **el** already conveys the “out of” relationship. No direct equivalent appears in the translation.
